# A Map of AI-for-Architecture Work {#sec-appendix-b-ai-for-architecture-map}

::: {.abstract}
This map consolidates the prior body of AI-for-architecture work that Architecture 2.0 builds on. It groups established results into families, maps each family to the principal life-cycle stages where cited work demonstrates activity, and shows how the discipline of an AI-native design system differs from any single method family. This synthesis serves as a positioning statement rather than an exhaustive literature survey.
:::

Machine learning has appeared in computer architecture for decades. Early work proposed learned in-chip mechanisms and models of architectural design spaces. More recent systems couple learned methods directly to simulators, compilers, and implementation tools. The families below form the foundation on which this work builds; because existing literature already provides comprehensive surveys [@ChenPenneyJimenez2020AIArchitecture], this map offers a positioning aid instead (@tbl-ai-arch-map).

## Three Claim Regimes

A cited result supports a claim only of the kind its family can make, and most families fall into one of three regimes. In the mechanism regime a learned component sits inside the hardware and is judged against the mechanism's own budget: mispredict rate at fixed storage and latency, coverage at fixed prefetch bandwidth. In the design-space-model regime a learned model approximates an expensive tool and is judged by its predictive fidelity against that tool over the region the search will visit. In the workflow regime the learned component participates in the design process itself, proposing, scheduling, placing, or generating, and the result must be judged at the level of the architecture study it contributed to rather than by the artifact it produced. Benchmarks, datasets, and shared simulators sit beside the three as evaluation infrastructure; they make no design claim of their own, and each grades work at one layer of the stack. Confusing the regimes is how a bounded branch-prediction result comes to be cited as evidence that an agent can be trusted with a floorplan. @tbl-ai-arch-map places each family in its regime and maps it to the life-cycle stages where the cited work demonstrates activity.

| **Family of work** | **Representative results** | **Claim regime** | **Principal life-cycle stages demonstrated** | **Developed in** | **Key sources** |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **Learned in-chip components** | Perceptron branch predictors and reinforcement learning prefetchers (Pythia, Berti), where learning is embedded in the mechanism itself and does a bounded tactical job | Mechanism | Implement, Evaluate | @sec-moonshot, @sec-methods-generation-prediction-optimization | [@JimenezLin2001Perceptron; @ChenPenneyJimenez2020AIArchitecture; @BeraEtAl2021Pythia; @NavarroTorresEtAl2022Berti] |
| **Learned cost models and predictive DSE** | Surrogates and regression models that predict performance and power across a design-space exploration (DSE) environment from cheap features | Design-space model | Explore, Evaluate | @sec-data-representations-world-models, @sec-methods-generation-prediction-optimization | [@IpekEtAl2006PredictiveDSE; @LeeBrooks2006RegressionModeling; @BaiEtAl2021BOOMExplorer] |

: **The unit of work in Architecture 2.0 is the architecture study and its reviewable claim, not any single family's artifact.** Each row names prior results, the principal life-cycle stages demonstrated by the cited work, and the chapters that develop it. The regime column names which kind of claim the family can support. The stage column uses three of the six life-cycle stage names that @sec-architecture-20-ontology defines (Formulate, Explore, Implement, Evaluate, Interpret, and Commit). {#tbl-ai-arch-map tbl-colwidths="[16,26,14,14,14,16]"}

These families are not mutually exclusive; a tool-using design-space search might invoke a learned cost model, orchestrate an autoscheduler, and emit candidate RTL within a single study. However, each family carries distinct physical and computational constraints. For example, the learned in-chip components family requires inference to fit strictly within the mechanism's silicon area and cycle latency budget. The perceptron predictor illustrates this tight physical boundary, operating within a $4\ \text{KB}$ hardware budget to deliver single-cycle branch predictions [@JimenezLin2001Perceptron].

These method families map directly to distinct regions of @fig-book-composition. Learned in-chip components, cost models, and autotuners occupy the intersection of computer architecture and machine learning. Reinforcement learning for physical design and LLM-driven RTL generation occupy the intersection of machine learning and electronic design automation (EDA). Learned models that predict routing hotspots and downstream congestion extend cost models into physical design [@Kahng2018Machine], providing fast early feedback before teams execute expensive downstream flows. Generated assertions and testbenches span both intersections as candidate verification collateral requiring independent review [@FangEtAl2025AssertLLM; @QiuEtAl2024AutoBench; @KangEtAl2024FVEval]. The stage distribution across @tbl-ai-arch-map exposes a structural asymmetry in existing literature: Explore appears in four rows, Implement in seven, and Evaluate in seven, yet no prior family demonstrates Formulate, Interpret, or Commit. A complete architecture study must supply those missing responsibilities under human authority.

What separates Architecture 2.0 from any single method family is the unit of work. Prior literature evaluates bounded point outputs: a learned branch predictor modifies one microarchitectural mechanism, a placement agent optimizes one layout step, and an RTL generator produces one isolated code block. Architecture 2.0 takes the complete architecture study and its reviewable claim as the fundamental unit of engineering work. The question is never merely whether a model produced a plausible candidate artifact, but whether the complete, closed-loop process supports a technical decision that another architect can inspect, reproduce, and challenge.

## The Latent Architectural Space Map

Machine learning models do not operate directly on raw silicon. Instead, they transform discrete hardware artifacts (such as abstract syntax trees (ASTs), control-data flow graphs (CDFGs), place-and-route netlists, and memory instruction traces) into continuous or structured latent representations. Four primary paradigms organize this latent territory: Token and Code Embeddings, Graph and Topological Embeddings, Continuous Surrogate Spaces, and Policy State Spaces (@tbl-latent-space-map). Each paradigm requires an independent, evaluator-owned physical grounding path to prevent latent hallucinations, vacuous syntax, and proxy gaming from corrupting the architecture loop:

| **Latent Space Paradigm** | **Underlying Representation** | **Search and Inference Mechanism** | **Physical Grounding and Decoupling** | **Primary Latent Failure Mode** |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **Token and Code Embeddings** | High-dimensional dense vectors derived from LLM activations over Verilog, SystemC, or Triton DSL code | Autoregressive token sampling, temperature decoding, and beam search | Executable compilation via Verilator or Yosys and functional testbenches | **Hallucinated Syntax and Vacuous Syntax:** Generated code looks syntactically plausible but violates ABI, bit-width, or structural invariants. |
| **Graph and Topological Embeddings** | Node and edge embeddings (GNNs, Hypergraphs) capturing spatial connectivity, CDFGs, or netlist floorplans | Node classification, edge prediction, and spatial clustering | Physical place-and-route tools via OpenROAD or Synopsys Innovus and static timing analyzers via OpenSTA | **Nonroutable Clustering:** Surrogates cluster macros optimally in graph space, but extracted physical layouts collapse under severe metal layer congestion. |
| **Continuous Surrogate and DSE Spaces** | Low-dimensional continuous manifolds mapping discrete architecture configurations (cache size, pipeline depth, bus width) to scalar power, performance, and area (PPA) estimates | Bayesian optimization (BO), Gaussian processes, and active learning acquisition functions | Cycle-accurate simulators like SCALE-Sim or gem5 and gate-level signoff via Ansys RedHawk-SC | **Out-of-Distribution Exploitation (Optimizer's Curse):** Optimizers select extreme latent points whose predicted gains are inflated by estimation error rather than by real PPA improvements [@SmithWinkler2006OptimizersCurse]. |
| **Policy and Reinforcement State Spaces** | Markov decision process (MDP) state-action vectors representing placement steps, tile schedules, or circuit transformations | deep Q-networks (DQNs), proximal policy optimization (PPO), and Monte Carlo tree search (MCTS) | Downstream physical design rule checking (DRC) and layout versus schematic (LVS) signoff and formal property checkers via Cadence JasperGold | **Reward Hacking:** The policy maximizes proxy reward functions (such as estimated wirelength) by injecting false timing paths or infeasible constraints. |

: **Mapping latent architectural spaces across representation paradigms.** Each paradigm embeds discrete hardware artifacts into continuous or graph-based latent vectors. Physical grounding through independent signoff engines remains mandatory to prevent latent hallucinations from reaching silicon. {#tbl-latent-space-map tbl-colwidths="[18,22,18,20,22]"}

These four latent paradigms connect to physical reality through structural decoupling, separating candidate generation in latent spaces from physical signoff in deterministic tools (@fig-latent-architectural-space-map). Placing an evaluator-owned physical signoff barrier between generative models and silicon commitment ensures that candidate representations are decoded, synthesized, and verified against physical ground truth.

![**The Latent Architectural Space Map decouples latent candidate generation from physical silicon signoff.** Machine learning models operate over four core representation paradigms (Token and Code Embeddings, Graph and Topological Embeddings, Continuous Surrogates, and Policy State Spaces). Each paradigm relies on an independent, evaluator-owned physical grounding path (Verilator, OpenROAD, SCALE-Sim, JasperGold) to prevent latent failure modes (Vacuous Syntax, Nonroutable Congestion, Optimizer's Curse, Reward Hacking) from reaching silicon. Verified candidates require human architect and commitment authority signoff across five clean physical signoff checks before tapeout freeze.](images/fig-latent-architectural-space-map){#fig-latent-architectural-space-map width="100%" fig-alt="Architecture diagram showing 4 Latent Space Paradigms at top, an Independent Evaluator-Owned Physical Signoff Barrier in the middle, and Verified Physical Silicon Signoff with Human Architect Commitment Authority at bottom."}

An independent, evaluator-owned grounding flow routes latent proposals through deterministic simulation, formal property verification, place-and-route, and static timing analysis. Before a candidate reaches the commitment authority it must clear the same signoff checks any design would: timing closure without unverified false-path or multicycle exceptions, power-domain and power-integrity verification, physical design rules and connectivity (DRC and LVS), clock- and reset-domain crossing verification, and electrothermal and packaging feasibility. Only candidates that clear all of them reach the commitment authority, whatever their fluency or their proxy score, because the physical and electrical rules that govern working silicon do not read the proxy.

## Candidates, Not Decisions

Within an AI-native design system, automated model outputs represent exploratory proposals rather than binding architectural choices. An autoscheduler's proposed schedule supports a performance claim only after measured execution on target hardware. A proposed placement requires downstream place-and-route, timing, power, and congestion checks. Generated RTL requires functional and implementation signoff. The accountable organization retains commitment authority, while verification and implementation owners retain signoff authority for their respective domains.

Candidates can mislead through false confidence or hidden total costs. Generated assertions can pass vacuously while checking nothing that matters, so apparent success is not independent evidence [@BeerEtAl2001Vacuity; @Clarke2018ModelChecking] (@sec-feedback-verification-trust). When evaluating macro-placement methods such as AlphaChip [@MirhoseiniEtAl2021GraphPlacement], a fair total-cost comparison must include the pretraining and fine-tuning runs used for the reported design, together with their compute [@ChengEtAl2026UpdatedAssessment]. Neither apparent verification success nor a favorable cost comparison replaces required domain signoff and organizational commitment.

## Scoped Claims of Landmark Systems

A landmark system is placed by the check that grades it, because the check bounds the claim. The shared infrastructure that makes such a check repeatable exists layer by layer. SPEC CPU2017 [@SPEC2017CPU] and MLPerf [@MattsonEtAl2020MLPerf] fix the workloads, gem5 [@BinkertEtAl2011Gem5] and FireSim [@KarandikarEtAl2018FireSim] supply cycle-level simulation and emulation on field-programmable gate arrays, and each lets an outside group rerun and dispute a result at its own layer. None of them carries a candidate from workload to signoff, so a result graded by one of them is a result at that layer and the claim it supports stops there. Four classes of check cover the public systems that this book cites (@tbl-existing-systems):

- **Exact or inexpensive verification.** When candidate solutions admit exact algebraic checks (such as AlphaTensor's matrix multiplication algorithms [@FawziEtAl2022AlphaTensor]) or bounded execution measurements (such as AutoTVM's tensor schedules [@ChenEtAl2018AutoTVM]), automated search can accept or reject candidates reliably. These checks enable efficient local optimization, but do not observe the broader system architecture.
- **Proxy and simulation feedback.** Broader exploration often relies on proxies (such as AlphaChip's wirelength estimates [@MirhoseiniEtAl2021GraphPlacement; @ChengEtAl2026UpdatedAssessment]) or cycle-level simulators (such as ArchGym [@KrishnanEtAl2023ArchGym], Apollo [@yazdanbakhsh2021apollo], and BOOM-Explorer [@BaiEtAl2021BOOMExplorer]). These methods expand the search space, but their claims remain bounded by the fidelity and blind spots of the underlying simulators.
- **Functional simulation, synthesis, and silicon.** Generated RTL evaluated through functional simulation (VerilogEval [@VerilogEval; @PinckneyEtAl2024RevisitingVerilogEval]) or post-synthesis metrics (RTLLM [@RTLLM]) tests implementation syntax and local quality, but stops short of physical signoff. While Chip-Chat [@BlockloveEtAl2023ChipChat] and Enlightenment-1 [@ChengEtAl2024AutomatedCPU] reached silicon, their flows relied on extensive manual repair or bounded Boolean synthesis rather than closed-loop multi-tool exploration.
- **Human ratings and proprietary reports.** Domain-adapted models (ChipNeMo [@LiuEtAl2023ChipNeMo]), tool-invoking wrappers (ChatEDA [@HeEtAl2024ChatEDA]), and commercial optimization engines (DSO.ai [@Synopsys2023DSOai]) demonstrate productive deployment, but their evaluations lack open matched baselines or complete public signoff data.

Each system supports only the claim its checks can falsify, and none of them provides the closed-loop capability the moonshot poses. @tbl-existing-systems records, for each, what it establishes and where its evidence stops:

| **System** | **What it establishes** | **The telltale limit** |
| --- | --- | --- |
| AlphaTensor [@FawziEtAl2022AlphaTensor] | Learned search improved a fifty-year-old matrix-multiplication count for 4-by-4 matrices modulo 2 | The algebraic construction admits an exact mathematical check, and a single scalar scores it |
| AutoTVM [@ChenEtAl2018AutoTVM] | Measured search can improve schedules when many candidates run quickly on real hardware | The result covers tensor-program schedules, where failures usually remain safely contained within the tuning run |
| AlphaChip [@MirhoseiniEtAl2021GraphPlacement; @ChengEtAl2026UpdatedAssessment] | A learned policy produces macro placements a production flow accepts | The reward relies on proxy wirelength and congestion, and the matched baseline remains disputed |
| ArchGym [@KrishnanEtAl2023ArchGym] | At equal sample budgets no search algorithm dominates, so the chosen harness and budget ultimately shape the result | Because every candidate is graded by a simulator, the result inherently adopts its fidelity limits |
| Apollo and BOOM-Explorer [@yazdanbakhsh2021apollo; @BaiEtAl2021BOOMExplorer] | Learned design-space exploration can successfully exploit domain-specific evidence | Apollo adapts learned representations across related accelerator spaces to reduce costly target evaluations; BOOM-Explorer uses an open-source core but depends on commercial tools and pays hours per sample |
| VerilogEval and RTLLM [@VerilogEval; @RTLLM] | RTL generation can be measured on shared benchmark tasks | VerilogEval emphasizes functional simulation; RTLLM adds post-synthesis quality metrics; neither reaches physical signoff |
| Chip-Chat and Enlightenment-1 [@BlockloveEtAl2023ChipChat; @ChengEtAl2024AutomatedCPU] | Generated logic has reached silicon, including a core that successfully boots Linux | One relies on extensive human-guided revision; the other synthesizes a processor from input-output examples with a provable accuracy bound, rather than the full multi-tool system-architecture capability the moonshot poses |
| ChatEDA [@HeEtAl2024ChatEDA] | An agent can plan and invoke a real tool flow directly from stated intent | The benchmark checks tool execution and human-rated request fulfillment on 50 ChatEDA-Bench tasks using a simplified OpenROAD wrapper, lacking independent functional correctness or complete signoff |
| ChipNeMo [@LiuEtAl2023ChipNeMo] | Domain adaptation can improve selected internal engineering tasks | The gains remain task-specific, general models stay stronger on certain subtasks, and outsiders cannot reproduce the proprietary evaluation |
| DSO.ai [@Synopsys2023DSOai] | Learned flow-parameter search has reached 100 vendor-reported commercial tapeouts | The evidence standard remains a vendor report, lacking a public methodology or matched baseline |

: **The strength of each result depends on its scope and how it is evaluated.** Exact, inexpensive checks support strong scoped claims, whereas narrow measurements, proxies, weak baselines, and hidden supporting data, methods, or artifacts all limit what architects can conclude. {#tbl-existing-systems tbl-colwidths="[22,38,40]"}

The table places claims; it does not rank systems. Anchoring each result to the check that graded it shows where the claim stops and where physical signoff and a named human decision must take over.
